```yaml
name: Performance Benchmark

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

concurrency:
  group: perf-benchmark-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  pull-requests: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  benchmark:
    name: Performance Benchmark
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10

    steps:
      - name: Checkout PR branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          path: pr-branch

      - name: Checkout main branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          path: main-branch

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - name: Build PR branch
        working-directory: pr-branch
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      - name: Build main branch
        working-directory: main-branch
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build

      - name: Run Benchmarks
        id: benchmark
        run: |
          # Function to run benchmark for a specific directory
          run_benchmark() {
            local dir=$1
            local runs=5
            local warmups=2
            local times=()
            
            echo "Running warmup runs in $dir..."
            for i in $(seq 1 $warmups); do
              cd $dir
              node dist/index.js --output-format json > /dev/null 2>&1
            done
            
            echo "Running measured runs in $dir..."
            for i in $(seq 1 $runs); do
              cd $dir
              # Use time command to get real time in seconds with high precision
              local start_time=$(date +%s%N)
              node dist/index.js --output-format json > /dev/null 2>&1
              local end_time=$(date +%s%N)
              local elapsed=$(( (end_time - start_time) / 1000000 )) # milliseconds
              times+=($elapsed)
            done
            
            # Sort times and find median
            IFS=$'\n' sorted=($(sort -n <<<"${times[*]}")); unset IFS
            local median=${sorted[$((runs / 2))]}
            echo "$median"
          }

          # Run benchmarks
          PR_TIME=$(run_benchmark "pr-branch")
          MAIN_TIME=$(run_benchmark "main-branch")
          
          # Calculate difference
          DIFF_MS=$((PR_TIME - MAIN_TIME))
          DIFF_S=$(echo "scale=2; $DIFF_MS / 1000" | bc)
          
          # Calculate percentage difference
          if [ "$MAIN_TIME" -ne 0 ]; then
            PERCENT=$(echo "scale=1; ($DIFF_MS * 100) / $MAIN_TIME" | bc)
          else
            PERCENT="0.0"
          fi
          
          # Determine sign for display
          if [ "$DIFF_MS" -ge 0 ]; then
            SIGN="+"
          else
            SIGN=""
          fi
          
          # Format output for comment
          PR_TIME_S=$(echo "scale=2; $PR_TIME / 1000" | bc)
          MAIN_TIME_S=$(echo "scale=2; $MAIN_TIME / 1000" | bc)
          
          # Create comment body
          COMMENT_BODY="| | Time |
|---|---:|
| PR branch | ${PR_TIME_S}s |
| main branch | ${MAIN_TIME_S}s |
| **Diff** | **${SIGN}${DIFF_S}s (${SIGN}${PERCENT}%)** |"

          # Output results for next steps
          echo "pr_time_s=${PR_TIME_S}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "main_time_s=${MAIN_TIME_S}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "diff_s=${DIFF_S}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "percent=${PERCENT}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "sign=${SIGN}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "comment_body<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "$COMMENT_BODY" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Post Benchmark Comment
        uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@v2
        with:
          header: perf-benchmark
          message: |
            ## Performance Benchmark Results
            
            ${{ steps.benchmark.outputs.comment_body }}
            
            *Note: Benchmarks are run on a single runner and may vary. Results represent median of 5 runs after 2 warmups.*
```
